Creating  an E mergency  B oard to I n­
vestigate  a D ispute  B etween  the 
R a ilw a y Express A gency , I nc., and 
C erta in of I ts E mployees
W HEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Railway Express Agency, Inc., a  
carrier, and certain of its employees rep­
resented by the Brotherhood of Railway  
and Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers  
and Station Employes, a labor organiza­
tion; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a section of the country of  
essential transportation service:
NO W , THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U . S. C . 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate the said dispute. No  
m em ber of the said board shall be  
Pecuniarily or otherwise interested in  
any organization of railway employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
A s provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
m ade by the Railway Express Agency,  
Inc., or by its employees, in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 10509 is a single-paragraph Railway Labor Act section 10 emergency board order. Its only commands are creation of the board, a thirty-day report deadline and a recited statutory standstill. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (report deadline, option C) none of those ends the order; the first held end is the express revocation by EO 12553 on 1986-02-25 (signature date, no effective-date wording). The board's report date 1954-02-17 is a spent fact recorded in the clause reason. Savings: none found in EO 12553 or in the order itself. Searches: U.S. Code and eCFR number-citation searches found no hit for this order; the OFR disposition-note search lists only the EO 12553 revocation in the chain.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked for an earlier end: (1) the order's own terms contain a report deadline and a post-report standstill but no sunset, so the report and standstill dates are spent facts and not ends under the report-deadline ruling; (2) no extension, amendment or revocation of EO 10509 other than EO 12553 appears in the dossier chain or in the number-citation scan of held texts; the report-time extensions described in the held report (where a report is held) were stipulations approved by the President, not held instruments, and affect only the deadline; (3) a general later rule is not treated as an end, only EO 12553, which names the order by number.","independent_command_check":"The standstill is recited as provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, so any no-change duty it describes arises under that statute and not only from the order; by the order's own terms it ran only to thirty days after the board's report, which was long before 1986. The order creates no continuing right, office or appropriation. No other command in the order survives the board's report.","savings_check":"The text of EO 12553 contains no savings, exception, effective-date or notwithstanding wording (the held text was searched for those terms). The board's investigation, report and the standstill were spent in the 1950s, and the order created no accrued right or later-effective duty. The statute the order invokes is not affected by revoking the order.","scope_check":"One clause covers the whole order; the order has no partial-scope command, no exception and no delayed effective date. reviews.reasons: The genuine claim differs from the planted control in three dates: board first_end 1954-02-17, standstill first_end 1954-03-19 and whole_order_end 1954-03-19. Hashes and every quoted span, including the source note, re-checked and match. Identity: the held 18 FR 8471 text is EO 10509, signed Dwight D. Eisenhower, The White House, December 16, 1953 (F. R. Doc. 53-10596); the two-clause inventory covers the whole operative text. The held PEB 105 report (NMB Case A-4358) names EO 10509 dated December 16, 1953 on its cover and in the letter; the cover's date line reads FEBRUARY 17, 1954, and the rendered page image of the letter reads February 17, 1954, so the text layer's 'February 27,1964' is an OCR error and no conflict arises under D-20261125-board-cover-date, which the claim applies and discloses. Board clause ended by completion of its task on 1954-02-17; the no-change sentence ended at the end of 1954-03-19 (inclusive; exclusive 1954-03-18 stated); whole_order_end equals the later. The stipulated extension to February 17, 1954 moved only the deadline. EO 12553 lists the order, has no saving provision and is kept as the formal disposition; OFR notes are only the EO 12553 revocation notes; no earlier end is held. Savings none.

savings_residuals.reason: The held text of EO 12553 contains no savings, transition or exception wording reaching EO:10509 (read in full for such wording; the only hits are subject lines in its tables). This claim ends the board clause on 1954-02-17 and the no-change period on 1954-03-19, both before that revocation, and the order created no appointment, transfer or right that survives independently of it; no held source shows a continuing independent effect.
